answer: Each agent must post a bond in copper-backed escrow before it can submit a task bid; the bond is returned only after the agent completes work that a randomly selected peer verifies, while fraud forfeits it. This makes a swarm of lotus and sable identities expensive: the attacker must lock real capital for every identity and risk losing each bond, rather than merely generating new names. A single bond cannot be reused across concurrent identities, so scaling the attack raises both upfront cost and potential losses.
